title: Einstein’s Biggest Mistake | The Cosmological Constant
description:
Albert Einstein, often hailed as the greatest scientist of all time, once admitted to making a blunder — but the story didn’t end there.

In 1915, Einstein introduced his theory of general relativity, revolutionizing how we understand gravity. But when applying it to the cosmos, he assumed the universe was static and unchanging, the accepted view of his time. To make this work, he added a new term to his equations: the cosmological constant (Λ). This “fix” was later rejected when Edwin Hubble showed the universe is expanding. Einstein reportedly called this his “greatest blunder.”

Yet decades later, the accelerated expansion of the universe was discovered. Enter dark energy — an unknown force pushing galaxies apart. Suddenly, Einstein’s “mistake” was resurrected as a crucial element of modern cosmology. Today, the cosmological constant plays a starring role in the ΛCDM model, the standard model of the universe.

We also explore contributions from Willem de Sitter, Alexander Friedmann, Georges Lemaître, and how science self-corrects, unlike religion. From supernovae observations in 1998 to Lucas Lombriser’s multiverse twist, the story of Einstein’s blunder is still unfolding.

If you’ve searched for Einstein’s blunder explained, cosmological constant, dark energy, expanding universe, Einstein mistakes, or ΛCDM model, this video breaks it all down in simple terms.
